change_scope: Explicit first question-version2 correction, not an answer-only repair. Retain the literal single-mark promise for every positive N, including N=1, and assess/refute the predecessor's universal normalized-unmarked-plane demand at that endpoint. Preserve the two reflections, their order, the interior angle/power target, and every other contract field. question: Keep the original promise of exactly one marked basis state among N states, with no exclusion of the positive endpoint N=1. Put g=|marked>, psi=N^(-1/2) sum_x |x>, R_g=I-2|g><g| and R_psi=2|psi><psi|-I, with Grover iterate G=R_psi R_g (marked flip first). Assess the predecessor's request to work in a two-dimensional real plane containing a normalized uniform superposition of all unmarked states for every allowed N: is that object defined at N=1? For N>1 construct the normalized unmarked state b and derive the exact matrix of G in the ordered basis (g,b). Define phi in (0,pi/2] by sin(phi)=1/sqrt(N), call 2phi the full iteration angle, distinguish its signed Cartesian orientation in (g,b) from the angle measured from b toward g, and prove the signed marked coefficient after k>=0 iterations is sin((2k+1)phi). Treat N=1 directly at the operator/state level without inventing a bad vector or a two-dimensional plane; say precisely which scalar formula survives and which geometric assertion fails. Do not infer that ordinary integer pi-phase iterations achieve arbitrarily near-unit success for every N.
reference_answer: The old universal two-dimensional-plane request is not defined at the allowed endpoint N=1: the unmarked sum is zero, and a zero vector cannot be normalized. This must be assessed, not silently removed by assuming N>=2. For N>1 define b=(N-1)^(-1/2) sum_{x unmarked}|x>. Then g,b are orthonormal and psi=s g+c b with s=sin(phi)=1/sqrt(N), c=cos(phi)=sqrt((N-1)/N). Both reflections preserve this real plane. In the ordered basis (g,b), R_g=diag(-1,1), and R_psi=[[2s^2-1,2sc],[2sc,2c^2-1]]. Multiplying in the stipulated order gives G=[[1-2s^2,2sc],[-2sc,2c^2-1]]=[[cos(2phi),sin(2phi)],[-sin(2phi),cos(2phi)]]. It is the Cartesian rotation by -2phi in this ordered basis. Equivalently, parameterizing a vector as sin(alpha)g+cos(alpha)b measures alpha from b toward g; multiplication advances alpha to alpha+2phi. The mirror axes are b for R_g and psi for R_psi and differ by phi, giving the same magnitude 2phi with this orientation. Thus Gg=cos(2phi)g-sin(2phi)b and Gb=sin(2phi)g+cos(2phi)b. The addition formulas, or induction starting at alpha=phi, give G^k psi=sin((2k+1)phi)g+cos((2k+1)phi)b for every integer k>=0. The marked coefficient is signed; its measurement probability is sin^2((2k+1)phi), and its absolute amplitude magnitude is the absolute value of that sine. At N=1, psi=g, R_psi=I on the one-dimensional space and R_g=-I, so G=-I and G^k psi=(-1)^k g exactly. Taking phi=pi/2, sin((2k+1)phi)=(-1)^k still matches the exact signed coefficient, but there is no bad component, mirror-axis comparison or planar rotation to prove. The mark is already found with probability one at k=0. N=0 is incompatible with the unique-mark promise, not an extra excluded search case. Ordinary integer iterations do not guarantee arbitrarily high success for all nontrivial sizes: N=2 has phi=pi/4 and success exactly1/2 for every integer k. Efficient implementation, finite-bit synthesis and any extra cleanup or success boosting are outside this algebraic question. This is an explicit endpoint-corrected question, not proof of the original universal plane assertion.

rubric.criterion: Explicitly identifies/refutes the nonexistent normalized unmarked vector and two-dimensional plane at N=1, without adding N>=2 as a standing premise.
For N>1 constructs orthonormal g,b and psi=sin(phi)g+cos(phi)b; obtains both reflection matrices and their stipulated product with correct signs.
Distinguishes Cartesian angle -2phi in basis(g,b) from advancement +2phi measured from b toward g, and derives the all-k signed sine/cosine action.
Treats N=1 as G=-I with exact (-1)^k coefficient, distinguishes signed coefficient/magnitude/probability, and rejects a universal near-unit integer-iteration guarantee using N=2.

exposition.core_summary: The Grover plane exists only when the bad component is nonzero. For N>1 the exact oriented rotation yields the odd-multiple sine; at N=1 G=-I preserves success while the two-dimensional construction is undefined.

semantic_steps.claim: Set sin(phi)=1/sqrt(N). For N>1 construct the normalized bad vector and decompose psi; at N=1 that vector is undefined, not a new hypothesis.
On the nontrivial plane the marked flip is diag(-1,1); at N=1 it is the scalar -I.
The uniform reflection fixes psi and negates its orthogonal line; at N=1 it is I on the sole line.
The two nontrivial mirror axes differ by phi, yielding angle magnitude2phi, with orientation measured explicitly rather than inferred.
The ordered(g,b) product is [[cos2phi,sin2phi],[-sin2phi,cos2phi]]; the endpoint instead has G=-I.
All k>=0 give signed marked coefficient sin((2k+1)phi), including (-1)^k at N=1, without a universal near-unit success claim.
